 all W.P.Nos. : Mrs.Hema Sampath
 Senior Counsel

 all W.P.Nos.

 COMMON ORDER
All these Writ Petitions have been filed challenging the award passed by the third respondent fixing compensation payable to the petitioners for the extension of National Highways.

2. The learned Senior Counsel appearing for the petitioners assailed the impugned order passed by the third respondent on the ground that while fixing the compensation for the lands of the petitioners acquired for extension of National Highways, the building standing in the acquired lands were not taken into consideration by the respondents mainly on the ground that the construction on Meenambal vs The District Collector on 10 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53851111/
2 the building had taken place, subsequent to the land acquisition notification.

3. The learned Senior Counsel appearing for the petitioners further submitted that in the impugned award, the third respondent considered the claim of the petitioners whose names are found place in the revenue records.

The learned Senior Counsel for the petitioners further stated that all the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis W.P.Nos.10185, 10213, 10219, 10224, 10231, 10236 & 10238 of 2023 petitioners belonged to very same family and it is the family property, therefore, all of them are having distinct interest in the property and the same has not been considered by the third respondent.

4. As per Section 3G (5) of the National Highways Act, any person aggrieved by the award passed by the Competent Authority determining the quantum of compensation payable can file an application before the Arbitrator appointed by the Central Government.

The questions raised by the learned Senior Counsel for the petitioners with regard to the timing of construction and with regard to the entitlement of the petitioners to receive compensation etc., are all question of facts which can be decided only based on the evidence to be let in by the parties.
Therefore, this Court cannot go into the questions raised by the petitioners in the writ jurisdiction.
However, the petitioners have an effective alternative remedy of seeking Arbitration under Section 3G (5) of the National Highways Act.

5. It is also brought to the notice of this Court that the impugned award copy was served on the petitioners only during June 2022 in response to the RTI query raised by the petitioners and the same can be gathered from the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis W.P.Nos.10185, 10213, 10219,
10224, 10231, 10236 & 10238 of 2023 proceedings of the third respondent dated 17.06.2022 in e/f/nj/be/45V- ep/v/m1-307-2022/
6.
Therefore, there is no impediment for the petitioners to file an application before the Arbitrator appointed by the Central Government.
It is not in dispute that the first respondent is the Arbitrator entitled to decide the application filed under Section 3G (5) of the National Highways Act.
Therefore, the petitioners are granted liberty to file a claim petition before the first respondent within a period of four weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this order.

The first respondent shall consider the claim petition of the petitioners in accordance with law as per the provisions of Arbitration and Conciliation Act and pass final award as expeditiously as possible preferably within a period of one year from the date of receipt of copy of this order.
7. With the above directions, these Writ Petitions are disposed of.
No costs.

Consequently,
connected Miscellaneous Petitions are closed.
8. As far as the quantum of compensation determined in respect of the lands, there is no dispute.

The dispute is only with regard to timing of https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis W.P.Nos.10185,
10213, 10219, 10224, 10231, 10236 & 10238 of 2023 constructions found in the said land and it's value.

Therefore, the petitioners are entitled to withdraw that portion of the compensation as determined by the third respondent after making appropriate application before the third respondent satisfying him with regard to the entitlement of the petitioners to receive the Meenambal vs The District Collector on 10 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53851111/
3 compensation.
